newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore August bank credit rises 17 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Singapore August bank credit rises 17 pct on year.

text.p: Bank credit to non-bank customers (in billions of Singapore dollars).
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its monthly report bank credit expanded at a slightly slower rate of 17 percent in August, compared with 18 percent the month before.
Loans growth in the manufacturing, transport and building and construction sectors rose by one percentage point each to 13 percent, 23 percent and 32 percent respectively.
"However, this was more than offset by slower growth in credit extended to the other major sectors," the report said.

Bank lending to the commerce sector grew by seven percent, compared with nine percent in July and that to financial institutions grew by 15 percent, compared with 17 percent. Growth of loans to professional and private individuals also moderated.
Finance companies' loans to non-bank customers continued to be slow, with growth declining to three percent in August after a slight pick-up in July.
"This reflected the 14 percent fall in hire-purchase financing, as lending for both motor-vehicle and consumer durable purchases declined sharply," the MAS said.
